IN  S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.51/1996  (Mohan Das Vs. State of Rajasthan)
Date of Order : 26.07.2016  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GOVERDHAN BARDHAR Mr. J.K. Chanda, for the petitioner.
Mr. L.R. Upadhyay, Public Prosecutor.
BY THE COURT

entities.text: S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.51/1996  (Mohan Das Vs. State of Rajasthan)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner by way of present revision petition under Section 397/401 Cr.P.C. has assailed the impugned judgment dated 24.01.1996 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge No.2, Jodhpur (hereinafter "the Appellate Court") in Criminal Appeal No.2/1996 whereby the learned appellate Court has maintained the conviction but modified the sentence awarded to the petitioner by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jodhpur (hereinafter "the trial court") vide judgment dated 13.12.1995 in Cr. Case No.67/1987 for offence under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, 'PFA Act') and sentenced the petitioner to undergo six months' simple imprisonment alongwith fine of Rs. 1000/- and in default thereof to undergone one month's simple imprisonment.

For offence under Rule 50(1) of the PFA Rules, the petitioner was ordered to undergo ten days'
simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.300/- and in default thereof to further undergo three day's simple imprisonment.
Brief facts, giving rise to this revision petition are that on 29.06.1987, the Food Inspector took sample of Ghee from the S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.51/1996 (Mohan Das Vs. State of Rajasthan) petitioner's shop.

entities.text: S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.51/1996 (Mohan Das Vs. State of Rajasthan)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Upon sending the sample to the Public Analyst, it was found to be misbranded.
Accordingly, upon obtaining sanction from the competent authority, the case was registered against the accused-petitioner.
Before framing of charge, statement of Girish Narayan (PW-1) was recorded.

The learned trial Court framed charge against the petitioner for offence punishable under Section 7/16 of PFA and for offence under Rule 50(1) read with Section 7/16 of PFA Act and the accused denied the charge.

After conclusion of the prosecution evidence, statement of the accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
was recorded.

The learned trial Court, thereafter, heard final arguments and by its judgment dated 13.12.1995, convicted the accused-petitioner for offence under Section 7/16 of the Act and passed the sentence of one year's simple imprisonment with fine of Rs.2000/-.

In default of payment of fine,
the Court ordered that petitioner shall undergo three months' simple imprisonment.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the judgment of the learned trial Court, the petitioner approached the learned appellate Court.

The appellate Court although maintained the conviction for aforesaid offence but reduced the sentence from one year to six months as also fine from Rs.2,000/- to Rs,1000/- for offence under Section 7/16 of PFA Act.

The appellate court further S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.51/1996 (Mohan Das Vs. State of Rajasthan) reduced the sentence from ten days to three days' simple imprisonment in default of payment of fine of Rs.300/- for violation of Rule 50(1)
of PFA Rules.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the outset, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that he is not challenging the conviction of the petitioner for offence under Section 7/16 of the Act recorded by the learned trial court and affirmed by the learned appellate court but his only prayer is for issuance of direction to the State Government to consider case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner is not a habitual offender and therefore, his case for commutation of sentence can very well be considered by the Government under Section 433(d)
Cr.P.C.

In support of this plea, learned counsel has placed reliance on decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court and High Court in the case of N.Sukumaran Nair V/s. Food 4 Inspector, Mavelikara [1995 SC CANDID 80] and Deva V/s. State of Rajasthan [2015 2 RLW(Raj.) 1002; 2014 Supreme(Raj) 544].

entities.text: N.Sukumaran Nair V/s. Food 4 Inspector, Mavelikara [1995 SC CANDID 80]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Deva V/s. State of Rajasthan [2015 2 RLW(Raj.) 1002; 2014 Supreme(Raj) 544]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Public Prosecutor has not opposed the prayer in general and submitted that in some of the identical cases, directions have been issued by the Court for consideration of commutation of sentence.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.

It is not disputed that the petitioner is not a habitual offender and therefore, the prayer to examine the case of the petitioner for commutation of sentence is acceptable.
S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.51/1996 (Mohan Das Vs. State of Rajasthan)

sentences.text:
In N.Sukumaran (supra), Supreme Court examined the matter pertaining to offence under Section 7/16 of the Act on the touchstone of Section 433(d) Cr.P.C. and held :
"3.
The offence took place in the year 1984.
The appellant has been awarded six months' simple imprisonment and has also been ordered to pay a fine of Rs.1,000.00
Under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, "the appropriate government" is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine.
We think that this would be an appropriate case for commutation of sentence where almost a decade has gone by.

We, therefore, direct the appellant to deposit in the trial court a sum of Rs.6,000.00 as fine in commutation of the sentence of six months' simple imprisonment within a 5 period of six weeks form today and intimate to the appropriate government that such fine has been deposited.

On deposit of such Mohan Dass vs State Of Rajasthan on 26 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162486242/
2 fine, the State Government may formalise the matter by passing appropriate orders under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedures."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Deva(supra) following the verdict in N.Sukumaran (supra) and taking into account the fact that incident is too old, held as under :
"9.
The offence took place in the year 1981.
The accused petitioner has been awarded the imprisonment as indicated above.

Under Clause (d) of Section 433 of the Cr.P.C.
The appropriate government is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine. 10.
I think that this would be an appropriate case for commutation of sentence where almost a decade has gone by.

I, therefore, direct the petitioner to deposit in the trial Court a sum of Rs.6,000/- as fine in commutation of the sentence of six months simple imprisonment within a period of six weeks from today and intimate to the appropriate government that such fine has been deposited.

On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalise the matter by passing appropriate orders; under Clause S.B. CRIMINAL REVISION PETITION NO.51/1996 (Mohan Das Vs. State of Rajasthan)
(d) of Section 433 of Cr.P.C.
Till then the petitioner will remain on same bail bonds."
Undisputedly, since conviction of the petitioner, there is nothing adverse against him so as to prove that he is involved in food adulteration.

In this view of the matter and considering the fact that incident has occurred about 29 years back, I deem it just and appropriate to direct the petitioner to deposit a sum of Rs.7,500/- as fine before learned trial Court in commutation of sentence of six month's and ten days' simple imprisonment for offence under Section 7/16 of the Act and Rule 50(1)
of PFA Rules respectively, within a period of two months from today.

After deposition of the aforesaid amount, the petitioner may intimate the appropriate Government so as to formalize the matter by passing appropriate orders; under Clause (d) of Section 433 Cr.P.C. Till then the matter is formalized by the State Government for passing appropriate orders for commutation of sentence,
the petitioner shall remain on the same bail bonds.
With these observations, the revision petition is disposed of.

(GOVERDHAN BARDHAR),J.
